answer: The protocol validates autonomous agents by reserving 1,000 distinct service slots, where a verifier demands exclusive occupancy of a jade-colored, secure cloud-edge slice to confirm identity. Agents must prove direct capacity-reservation via timed signals across a specific meadow of network switches, failing if pulses show relaying. The verifier revokes any slot if latency jitter exceeds the orchard-level threshold of 5ms. An honest participant pays 1x cost, while an attacker pays 1,000x for 1,000 isolated, non-pooled units. Fees are non-refundable to ensure rigorous network commitment.
